subject: Trade-off between divergence and Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information

messages.author: 1512be96805145af
messages.subject: Trade-off between divergence and Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information
parts:
I’m trying to replicate the soil carbon example given online at http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/soil-knit.html. When I run the model with the control parameters given in the example (adapt = 0.9) I get a warning message of having divergent transitions. When I tweak the control parameters to eliminate divergence (say, set adapt = 0.999), I get a different warning of having low Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information. I can’t seem to get around both of the warnings, only one or the other.

Has anyone run into and solved this trade-off between divergence and missing information?

I’ve replicated the model exactly from the example, with the only change being that I modified the original integrate_ode() to integrate_ode_bdf(). Though I have the same problems if I use integrate_ode_rk45(). My .stan and .R files are attached.

Thanks,

Steve Wood

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trade-off between divergence and Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information
parts:
It’s not that there is a trade off between divergences and low E-BFMI,
rather the divergences are masking a low E-BFMI.  Remember that
divergences indicate that you’re not able to explore the entire target
distribution, and that incomplete exploration can give you inaccurate
E-BFMI estimates.  Only when you increase adapt_delta and the 
exploration becomes more accurate does the accurate E-BFMI
emerge!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trade-off between divergence and Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information
parts:
The small E-BFMI typically indicate heavy tails, so it could
be that the priors are not sufficiently identifying the model.
Not unlikely for a complex ODE-based system.

messages.author: fca1b10a695129c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trade-off between divergence and Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information
parts:
In the case study attached, I have examples for both real and simulated data. For real data, with adapt_delta=0.9999 and stepsize=0.003 (four chains, 500 iterations each), I do not get any warning. Also, for more sophisticated models with hierarchical structure (like the ones in this repo) with sufficiently high adapt_delta, I don't get any warnings. 

Milad
